rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=8, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=True, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE_ITER=6 (the stable share=True, lr=5e-3 config that produced the BEST SSIM 0.8185 / hr 0.0). TRAJECTORY (SSIM/hr): iter-1 K=10 0.2855/0; iter-2 K=30 0.2855/0 (depth FALSIFIED at the frozen-step regime, byte-identical); iter-3 step=1e-8 0.8137/0 (LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH); iter-4 step=1e-5 share=F 0.6949/0 (per-step RUNAWAY into clamp); iter-5 step=1e-5 share=T 0.6074/0 (per-step runaway fixed but LAMBDA runaway); iter-6 lr 5e-2->5e-3 0.8185/0 (lambda runaway tamed -> SSIM recovered to the FBP passthrough floor but did NOT exceed it). BEST SSIM 0.8185 (iter-6); hr=0.0 EVERY iter. MAPPED KNOBS: tv_step_init bracketed {1e-2 saturate, 1e-8 passthrough, 1e-5 active-basin}; tv_share_steps {F runaway, T stable}; tv_lr {5e-2 over-drives, 5e-3 stable}; tv_K raised 10->30 ONLY at the FROZEN-step regime (iter-1/2, where it was provably inert). HELD CONSTANT ALL CAMPAIGN: tv_lambda_init=1e-3, epochs=8, train_n=40, AND tv_K has NEVER been probed DOWN, and NEVER re-probed at the now-stable (share=T, step=1e-5, lr=5e-3) regime. LIMITER: iter-6 sits EXACTLY at the LD-FBP passthrough floor (0.8185 ~= the 0.8137/~0.81 floor) -> the trained K=30 GD with the settled small-lambda is a near-identity map on fbp_init that neither helps NOR hurts. The question the campaign has NOT answered: is supervised-TV FBP-bounded along the DEPTH axis at the stable regime? This campaign overturned FOUR assumed ceilings via a single untried lever, and TWICE that lever was unroll-DEPTH-DOWN (itnet itnet_k 3->1, hammernik_vn vn_T 5->2). The TV analog (tv_K DOWN) has NEVER been run at a regime where training is stable. ONE KNOB CHANGED (from BASE_ITER=6): tv_K 30 -> 8 (depth-DOWN, the genuinely-untried structural lever). All else IDENTICAL to iter-6 (tv_share_steps=True, tv_step_init=1e-5, tv_lr=5e-3, tv_lambda_init=1e-3, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: with FEWER unrolled GD steps the cumulative TV smoothing is reduced, so the supervised optimizer can fit a SHARPER trained step/lambda that applies a few targeted data-consistency corrections while staying closer to the sharp FBP init -- if supervised-TV has ANY headroom above its own FBP, a shallow unroll is structurally where it would surface (mirroring the itnet/hammernik_vn depth-DOWN breakouts), lifting SSIM ABOVE 0.8185 and clearing hr>0. NUMERIC FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays <= 0.8185 with hr=0.0 at K=8, depth-DOWN is exhausted at the stable regime -> the LAST structural lever is retired and supervised-unrolled-TV is CONFIRMED FBP-bounded on real Mayo 2304-view LDCT under the config-only contract (the shared solvers raw unnormalized-adjoint back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT and STOP at iter-7. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score = 1200s): tv_K 30->8 STRICTLY LOWERS compute (fewer unroll steps per train+val pass; fixed overhead = data load + 214-slice FBP precompute dominates) -> WELL under iter-6 measured 911.5s, comfortable margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. PREDICTED iter-7: SSIM ~0.80-0.86, hr most-likely 0.0 (a single global TV weight over a near-complete inverse is a structurally weak image-domain prior on real LDCT noise, regardless of depth); small chance hr 0.0-0.05 if shallow depth lets a sharper trained step beat the passthrough.
